# /crav1-ado-sync

[All skills](../skills.md) · Walkthrough: [Feature candidates](../../from-feature-candidates.md) · Playbook: [`SKILL.md`](../../../.cursor/skills/crav1/crav1-ado-sync/SKILL.md)

## Purpose

Keep specs and Azure Boards in step; asks suggest Features, push Features, push tasks, pull tasks, or pull spec changes.

**[`/crav1-ado-sync`](crav1-ado-sync.md)** opens with one question: suggest Features (read only), push Features, push tasks, pull task changes, or pull spec changes from Features. It skips the question when the message says which. Every write to Azure Boards still needs a yes. It replaces feature-candidates, specs-to-ado, tasks-to-ado, ado-to-tasks, and ado-to-specs; their rules are kept as branches.

Suggest Features (was `/crav1-feature-candidates`): Lists Feature candidates from the landscape, the specs, research, sources, and open notes. Writes nothing unless the user asks for a file.

Suggest Features (was `/crav1-feature-candidates`): Titles say what the work is, for example 'Email service: DA Nord Pool MCR via mailbox'. Each candidate has the same labelled lines (Target date (with its source), Spec, Description, Open blockers/questions as bullets with who and when where the docs say, and Order/priority). Descriptions are full paragraphs with context, who does what, related task-list items, and quotes with names and dates, and nothing the docs do not state.

Push Features (was `/crav1-specs-to-ado`): Sends picked candidates to Azure Boards as Features after a yes, then writes the id onto the spec.

Push Features (was `/crav1-specs-to-ado`): Before the preview it strips spec paths, `docs/sources/` folders, and spec references from the candidate text, so nothing sent to Azure Boards points at the specs repo.

Push Features (was `/crav1-specs-to-ado`): Each implementation repo has its own work item home, the `Work items go to` column in `docs/system/repos.md` (`ADO: <org>/<project>`), asked once per repo the first time and written only after the answer. A spec whose repos are in several homes gets one Feature in each, previewed and sent on its own yes, linked in the same org or mentioned in plain text across orgs. Id lines end with `(ADO: <org>/<project>)`.

Push tasks (was `/crav1-tasks-to-ado`): Pick one spec that already has a Feature id in `work-item.md`. Every task in its `tasks.md` is listed, numbered, and you pick by number or all. The child work item type is asked once and saved as a line in `docs/environments/marks.md`, with the type's done state (Closed on Agile, Done on Scrum and Basic); edit a line to change it. The question marks the type on the requirement backlog level directly under Feature as recommended (User Story on Agile, Product Backlog Item on Scrum, Issue on Basic, Requirement on CMMI), and gives none when the levels cannot be read.

Push tasks (was `/crav1-tasks-to-ado`): Each task is previewed as a child of the Feature: a fuller title that says what the work is, State New (or the done state when the box is ticked), Iteration and Priority blank, tags for the slice and the code repos, the owner when the docs state one, a fuller description (what, why, who, decisions with quotes, names, and dates, related items, open blockers or none recorded), and the task's verify line as acceptance. File paths, line numbers, spec references, and kit names are stripped; code repo names stay; the specs repo is never mentioned.

Push tasks (was `/crav1-tasks-to-ado`): On an update, a box ticked since the item was sent offers moving it to the done state, and an unticked box on a closed item offers a reopen to New, each only on a yes. A disagreement the `tasks.md` history does not explain shows both sides and asks each time. The kit never sets Active or Resolved and never sends Reason.

Push tasks (was `/crav1-tasks-to-ado`): Each task goes to its repo's work item home and its parent is the Feature in that home. A task with no clear repo, or with repos in different homes, is asked about. The child type and done state are saved per home in `docs/environments/marks.md`.

Pull tasks (was `/crav1-ado-to-tasks`): Pick a spec with task lines in `work-item.md`, or all. Every recorded task item is read back (State, title, description, acceptance, Assigned To, comments, history) and only what differs from the spec and `tasks.md` is shown, plus child items under the Feature that no task line records.

Pull tasks (was `/crav1-ado-to-tasks`): Each difference is kept or dismissed, fresh every run. Kept changes go in through [`/crav1-add-to-spec`](crav1-add-to-spec.md). A task in the done state in Azure Boards ticks its box only on your yes; one reopened there unticks a ticked box only on your yes. Each id is read in its own work item home; one not found is reported as moved or missing. A new child is added as a task, with its id recorded in `work-item.md`, only on your yes. It never writes a field back; a reply comment is stripped and posted only on yes.

Pull spec changes (was `/crav1-ado-to-specs`): Reads Azure Boards Features back and shows what differs. A kept change goes through [`/crav1-add-to-spec`](crav1-add-to-spec.md). A reply comment is posted only after a yes.

Pull spec changes (was `/crav1-ado-to-specs`): Each id is read in its own work item home. An id not found there is reported as moved or missing, and it asks before searching other projects.

## Runs when

Specs and Azure Boards should match. Called by the user and by [`/crav1-ado-sync`](crav1-ado-sync.md).

## Reads

In short: Suggest Features: The landscape, the specs, research, and sources; Push Features: The org, the project, and the candidate list; Push tasks: The org, the project, the spec's Feature id, and its `tasks.md`; Pull tasks: The task items a spec records, and the Feature's children; Pull spec changes: Recorded Feature ids, or the ids named.

Suggest Features: Reads `docs/system/landscape.md` (the spec index, Ideas, Way of working, and code with no slice), `docs/system/repos.md`, the glossary, every `docs/specs/*/spec.md` (milestones, slices, open questions, and actions), `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, and `verify.md` where present, `docs/research/` and `docs/sources/` with each fact labelled by its source, a stale research note shown as stale, open notes in `docs/notes/` labelled as notes and not as candidates by themselves, each spec’s `work-item.md`, and the landscape “No spec yet in ADO” table. Push Features: Reads the org and project from `docs/environments/marks.md` or Azure DevOps URLs in `docs/system/repos.md`, checks `az` including the default install paths, checks that the project has the Feature work item type, reads the Feature fields before the preview, and reads the candidate list. When the type has Acceptance Criteria, the checks go there. When it does not, the checks go in the Description as an Acceptance checks list and that field is not sent. Push tasks: Reads the org and project from `docs/environments/marks.md` or Azure DevOps URLs in `docs/system/repos.md`, checks `az` the same way as [`/crav1-ado-sync`](crav1-ado-sync.md), reads the Feature id from `work-item.md`, every task in `tasks.md`, the saved child type line, the project's work item types on the first run, and the child type's fields. Pull tasks: Reads the org and project the same way as [`/crav1-ado-sync`](crav1-ado-sync.md), the task lines and the Feature line in `work-item.md`, every recorded task item with its comments and history, the child type's fields, and the Feature's children. Pull spec changes: Reads the ids in every `work-item.md` and the landscape “No spec yet in ADO” table, or only the ids the user names, then State, Priority, Target Date, Iteration, Assigned To, discussion comments, and history. It reads the checks from Acceptance Criteria when the Feature type has that field, and from the Acceptance checks list in the Description when it does not, so a match is not a change. Comments use api version `7.1-preview`, which `az devops invoke` can parse.

## Writes

In short: Suggest Features: Nothing unless the user asks for a file; Push Features: A Feature in Azure Boards after a yes, then its id in that spec's `work-item.md` or a landscape "No spec yet in ADO" row; Push tasks: Child work items in Azure Boards after a yes, then task lines in that spec's `work-item.md`; Pull tasks: Kept changes through [`/crav1-add-to-spec`](crav1-add-to-spec.md); a comment in Azure Boards after a yes; Pull spec changes: Nothing itself. A reply comment in Azure Boards only after a yes. Kept changes and answers go to the spec through [`/crav1-add-to-spec`](crav1-add-to-spec.md).

Suggest Features: Writes nothing unless the user asks for a file. Push Features: Writes a Feature only after the user says yes. After a Create, writing the new id into that spec’s `work-item.md` with its milestone or slice label, or a row on the landscape “No spec yet in ADO” table when the item has no spec, is required. Push tasks: Writes a child work item only after the user says yes, linked to the Feature as its parent. After a Create, appends `Work item: <id> — task: T<n> <short title>` to `work-item.md` (required). On the first run, appends the child type line and the done-state line to `docs/environments/marks.md`. Pull tasks: Writes the spec and `tasks.md` only through [`/crav1-add-to-spec`](crav1-add-to-spec.md) for kept changes, ticks a box or adds a task only after a yes, appends a task line to `work-item.md` for an added task, and posts a reply comment only after a yes. Pull spec changes: Writes nothing itself. A kept change and an answer the user gives go to the spec through [`/crav1-add-to-spec`](crav1-add-to-spec.md). A reply comment is posted only after the user says yes.

## Does not

Suggest Features: Leaves specs, Azure Boards, and commits alone. Push Features: Leaves the preview unedited, Iteration and Priority blank, and the specs repo out of anything sent. Push tasks: Leaves `tasks.md` without ids, the preview unedited, Iteration, Priority, and Reason unsent, Active to people, and the specs repo out of anything sent. Pull tasks: Leaves every Azure Boards field, `tasks.md` ids, and dismissed changes alone. Pull spec changes: Leaves a missing id unmatched.

Limits and exceptions: Suggest Features: a dated milestone or slice is one candidate. An undated spec with open work is one candidate. A spec that holds only open questions is marked questions only. An item with no spec is marked no spec yet. Done or retired with nothing open is skipped. A target date is given only when the docs state it. It does not start Specify, Plan, or Build. It is not a starter option. Push Features: a missing Feature type stops. An `az` failure, including a failed field read, states the issue, suggests a fix such as `az login`, and offers a skip. It does not guess. It does not show the `az` command. It does not install or log in. The closing output names the file written, says it is not committed yet, names [`/crav1-finalize-commit`](crav1-finalize-commit.md), and says a later run would offer Create again. If the write fails, it prints the line to add. It does not start Specify, Plan, or Build. It is not a starter option. Push tasks: a spec with no Feature id is not offered and names [`/crav1-ado-sync`](crav1-ado-sync.md). A re-run offers Update for a recorded task and shows only changed fields. Edits go into the spec first through [`/crav1-add-to-spec`](crav1-add-to-spec.md). An `az` failure states the issue, suggests a fix, and offers a skip. It does not commit. It is not a starter option. Pull tasks: a spec with no task lines names [`/crav1-ado-sync`](crav1-ado-sync.md). A missing id is reported as missing, not guessed. Dismiss is for this run only. It does not commit. It is not a starter option. Pull spec changes: dismissals start fresh each run. A no-spec-yet Feature names a starter such as [`/crav1-spark-to-spec`](crav1-spark-to-spec.md) and does not run it. When the spec has no answer, no reply is drafted and the question is offered as an open question. An `az` failure, including a failed field read, is handled the same way as [`/crav1-ado-sync`](crav1-ado-sync.md). It does not start Specify, Plan, or Build. It is not a starter option.
